annotation.title_clean: We Robot 2025: Connecting Global Robotics and AI Governance Experts in Canada
annotation.title_en: We Robot 2025: Connecting Global Robotics and AI Governance Experts in Canada
annotation.venue: Canadian Journal of Law and Technology
annotation.summary_en: Editors' introduction to the Canadian Journal of Law and Technology special issue for We Robot 2025, held at the University of Windsor. It describes the conference's interdisciplinary format and summarises seven papers. Topics include robotic agriculture and labour, expressive delivery robots, interoperable AI regulation, generated personal data, generative AI in contracts and facial recognition.
key_provisions_or_claims: We Robot 2025 was the first in-person We Robot conference held in Canada, at Windsor Law in April 2025
Meaningful robotics and AI regulation requires interdisciplinary engagement
Automation of farm work replicates historically oppressive, racialized labour practices (Venkatesh)
Expressive features of delivery robots shape public perception, which matters for policymakers (Schneider et al.)
Interoperability is explored as a concept for AI governance strategies (Raso)
